commander: Major General Edwin P. Parker, Jr.

notes: Event date: 5 February 1945 (Last Offensive ch. 4 p. 72-75: the 78th Division (Maj. Gen. Edwin P. Event definition: the division opens the attack of V Corps toward the Roer dams; the row is the first day of the attack and the village its first objective. Relationship: V Corps operational_control (from 2 Feb 45, narrative); XVIII Airborne Corps unspecified_subordination (from 3 Feb 45 to 11 Feb 45, CMH table); First Army assigned (from 2 Feb 45, CMH table); 12th Army Group assigned (from 9 Nov 44, CMH table). notes: Event date: 9 February 1945 (Last Offensive ch. 4 p. 81-82: at 1800 on 9 February the 1st Battalion, 309th Infantry, passed through the 311th Infantry and headed for the dam; by midnight the engineers had entered the inspection tunnel; the Germans had already destroyed the machinery and discharge valves). commander: Major General Edwin P. Parker, Jr.
current_activity: the 311th Infantry takes Honnef on the east bank of the Rhine, almost five miles north of the Remagen bridge
notes: Event date: 10 March 1945 (Last Offensive ch. 11 p. 225: as night fell on 10 March the 78th Division's 311th Infantry had advanced beyond the first phase line and taken Honnef, almost five miles north of the bridge; the CMH list has the command post at Erpel on 10 March). Event definition: the division expands the Remagen bridgehead northward; the row is the regiment's capture of the town. Relationship: III Corps unspecified_subordination (from 12 Feb 45 to 15 Mar 45, CMH table); First Army assigned (from 2 Feb 45, CMH table); 12th Army Group assigned (from 9 Nov 44, CMH table). The table entries start on the first row of the unbroken run (convention V-013). The CMH table has a single corps column and does not say assigned or attached for a corps. Location: Honnef, east bank of the Rhine. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Bad Honnef. Event support: moderate (single Green Book page; the CMH table lists III Corps from 12 February). Location support: moderate (named town). Review (spot check, 26 October 2026): the town was not clear at the end of 10 March in the sources checked and nothing is changed: old 'the 311th Infantry takes Honnef' on 10 March (Green Book p. 225, kept), new unchanged; the 78th Division after-action extracts for the Remagen bridgehead (allworldwars.com, 'The Remagen Bridgehead, March 7-17, 1945') have the 311th attacking Honnef on 10 March with resistance remaining at the northern end of the town at the day's end, a regimental account has the 1st Battalion in the town centre on 9 March, and the CMH Combat Chronicle (Army Almanac 1950) says the division took Honnef on 16 March. Read the row as the capture of most of the town, not a completed clearing.
